newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says sees Agrobanka branch sale soon.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says sees Agrobanka branch sale soon.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Tuesday it expected to decide in March at the latest on the sale of the Slovak branch troubled Czech Agrobanka a.s. to local firm A.G.B. a.s.
NBS spokesman Ivan Paska told Reuters that A.G.B., a newly established Bratislava-based firm, was the "only seriously interested entity" in the unit's purchase.
He said that an existing Slovak financial institution was one of A.G.B.'s owners, but he declined to elaborate.
"A.G.B. is still in the game...the transaction will probably happen, and the number of Slovak-owned banks will increase by one," Paska said. "We intend to resolve the issue in March at the latest."
"The Czech side is really interested in selling the branch," Paska said, adding that A.G.B.'s bid was incomplete and did not include a set basic capital for the bank.
The NBS had originally favoured a Slovak bank, and not an industrial company, as a partner to start operating as an independent bank.

Helena Jandikova, financial director of pharmaceutical maker Slovakofarma -- one of A.G.B.'s shareholders -- told Reuters that Slovakofarma, gas storage firm Nafta, insulation maker Izomat and pharmaceutical firm Biotika each planned to hold up to 15 percent in A.G.B.
She said the holder of the remaining stake was "uncertain".
The unit's officials revealed the plans to become a fully-independent bank from the beginning of 1997 last autumn.

The announcement came soon after the Czech parent was put under temporary forced administration by the Czech National Bank after experiencing liquidity problems stemming from the failure of another Czech bank, Kreditni Banka a.s..

Under the plan, the Czech parent would hold 34 percent, and five unspecified large Slovak companies from the chemical industry would share the remainder of the new bank's basic equity of one billion crowns.
Branislav Petroch, director of Slovak Agrobanka unit, declined to comment on the issue to Reuters on Tuesday.

But he was later quoted by the official news agency TASR as saying the Czech parent had signed an "agreement about a future purchase" with potential investors, adding it was too early to talk about the new bank's basic capital.
